stage_0_mechanics.purpose: verify action frequency, book reconstruction, fee arithmetic, timing semantics and settlement labels; no parameter selection or economic claim

stage_1_development.purpose: estimate effect direction and reject infeasible candidates cheaply

stage_2_selection.purpose: select at most one specification per candidate family with market-block purging

stage_3_sealed.purpose: one final after-cost out-of-sample evaluation per frozen candidate

stop_early_when: the mechanics cohort contains no executable action
a claimed strategy requires unavailable order-specific fill or queue evidence
the development result is nonpositive after exact fees and displayed-depth execution
the candidate fails probability calibration or is dominated by the executable market prior
a capture has an unrecoverable in-market book-integrity failure

execution_contract.book_price: consume recorded displayed depth; midpoint and last-trade fills are forbidden
execution_contract.fee: read the exact feeSchedule or verified per-market fee fields; apply the current venue formula and rounding; never hard-code the forum's 0.072 approximation
execution_contract.latency: evaluate recorded host receipt-to-decision latency plus venue taker delay and empirical order-response distributions at p50, p95 and p99
execution_contract.maker_fee: zero only when a post-only order is proven to have rested and its own fill is observed
execution_contract.maker_fill: no economic maker result from public books, public trades, touch assumptions or queue-position guesses
execution_contract.maker_rebate: zero in the primary result; only an actual market-specific paid rebate may be added in a separately reported attribution
execution_contract.market_liquidity_reward: zero unless the market exposes an active allocation and the exact order satisfies its size, spread, sidedness and duration requirements
execution_contract.order_atomicity: CLOB batch responses are independent; two separate outcome orders are never modeled as an atomic pair
execution_contract.resolution: official market-resolved winner and verified BTC TWAP60 market contract
execution_contract.slippage: book traversal plus the observed post-decision book at executable receipt; no fixed cents assumption

hypotheses.forum_claim: buying near 0.01-0.05 or 0.95-0.99 may capture panic liquidity or mispriced near-certain outcomes
hypotheses.primary_test: one taker entry held to official settlement after exact fee and latency
hypotheses.rejection_rule: reject if the market-block bootstrap lower bound of after-cost PnL is not positive or calibration is worse than the executable market prior

hypotheses.forum_claim: a sub-100ms selector may find late strong-but-not-certain favorites whose true settlement odds exceed their ask
hypotheses.primary_test: calibrated settlement-value model with the executable book prior as offset; enter only when model value exceeds ask plus exact fee and a frozen safety margin
hypotheses.latency_statement: sub-100ms is a hypothesis, not an assumption; venue delay and measured end-to-end latency remain binding
hypotheses.rejection_rule: reject accuracy that does not improve both calibrated probability loss and after-cost PnL versus the executable market prior

hypotheses.forum_claim: buy both outcomes below one dollar and merge the complete set
hypotheses.primary_test: submit two independently modeled FOK legs, then merge only the matched common quantity; charge exact fees and value every orphan immediately at executable liquidation depth
hypotheses.not_arbitrage_until: the full sequence remains positive after both independent order outcomes, fees, latency, partial or failed legs, orphan liquidation and merge completion
hypotheses.rejection_rule: reject if realistic sequential execution is nonpositive even when the same-receipt upper bound is positive

hypotheses.forum_claim: split one dollar into both outcomes, sell both above one dollar total, and earn spread or rebates
hypotheses.public_data_role: measure quote opportunity frequency, duration, depth, subsequent adverse-selection markouts and orphan-loss bounds only
economic_result_requires: known queue position or conservative queue-ahead reconstruction
hypotheses.orphan_policy: never average down; cap inventory before quoting; cancel stale complements; value and flatten only bot-owned unmatched exposure under a frozen loss budget
hypotheses.rejection_rule: no profitability result is permitted from public-book touch or assumed dual fills

hypotheses.forum_claim: a 20-minute extended move may reverse in the next five-minute window
hypotheses.primary_test: add frozen multi-horizon path-efficiency and reversal features to settlement value, then compare against the same executable market-prior baseline
hypotheses.reason_for_inclusion: directional reversal frequency alone is insufficient because the Polymarket ask may already price it
hypotheses.rejection_rule: reject unless incremental calibrated settlement value remains positive after exact execution costs

multiple_testing.selection_limit: at most one frozen specification per family
multiple_testing.sealed_confidence: market-block bootstrap 95 percent lower bound above zero after costs
multiple_testing.sealed_reuse: forbidden after one evaluation; any redesign requires a new future cohort

risk_boundaries.position_size: fixed five-share research unit, also report per-share economics
risk_boundaries.stale_or_untracked_positions: not applicable because this contract grants no execution authority

usable: specific price bands and execution hypotheses
warnings about maker adverse selection and orphan inventory
claims that can be independently replayed on prospective receipt-time books
not_evidence: directional tests based on candles rather than executable books
maker fills inferred from public quotes

source_research.finding: Current crypto taker fees use a market-specific schedule with a 0.07 category rate, while maker fees are zero and rebate percentages may change.
Selected crypto Up/Down markets can impose a 250 ms taker delay, which must be read from the market rather than assumed away.
A complete Yes/No set merges atomically to one pUSD, but acquiring the two legs through separate CLOB orders is not an atomic pair.
Polymarket explicitly recommends two-sided quoting, inventory skew, stale-quote cancellation, fill monitoring and a kill switch for market making.
Liquidity rewards are market-specific, relative to other makers, and require exact market settings; they are not a fixed spread subsidy.

terminal_claim_policy.positive_development_result: not an edge or profitability claim
terminal_claim_policy.positive_sealed_result: evidence of sample-bound after-cost edge, not guaranteed future profitability
terminal_claim_policy.negative_result: preserve and publish without parameter rescue on sealed data
